title: The command line

title: The command line
text: --target takes column task, separated colons: COL:regression continuous target, COL:classification:N target N classes. bare COL regression target. fields task modifiers order: log1p fits regression target log(1 + y) returns predictions column’s units. mask keeps plot label target: trains targets . default, drop, leaves plot run. integer sets number classes classification target. resolve train --help gives grammar: classification target needs class count: label column may hold text, habitat : loader codes labels integers, checkpoint keeps labels, predictions come back habitat names.
code: resolve train --help | grep -A 8 -e "--target SPEC" #>   --target SPEC               Target column and type. Repeat per target: #>                                 COL:regression          continuous target #>                                 COL:regression:log1p    fit on log1p(y), #>                                                         predictions inverted #>                                 COL:classification:N    N-class target #>                               A bare COL means COL:regression. Append :mask to #>                               keep plots that lack this label: they train the #>                               other targets only (default :drop leaves them out). #>   --encoding V                Species encoding: hash, embed, sparse, rank_pool, transformer (default: hash) resolve train --header plots.csv --species species.csv \   --species-id species --target habitat:classification --output model.pt #> RESOLVE Training #> ================ #> Error: --target habitat:classification: classification needs a class count >= 2, e.g. habitat:classification:9

title: The command line
text: default run holds 20 % plots, drawn random, stops loss improved --patience epochs (50 default). --test-size sets fraction. --seed (42 default) seeds starting weights, held-draw, order training plots drawn cross-validation folds. CPU, two runs flags seed train model, predictions match: GPU, also pass ---cudnn-benchmark: turns cuDNN autotuner, default can make two runs differ. --stopping-plots holds plots file names instead, one identifier per line: spatial block, another survey, fold published protocol selects epoch . best epoch final metrics read exactly plots. held-plots north 47° latitude: --stopping-plots --test-size exclude . refit every plot, fix length run advance hold nothing : --fixed-epochs N --test-size 0 trains exactly N epochs --max-epochs schedule keeps final weights. nothing held , run reports metrics.
code: for run in a b; do   resolve train --header plots.csv --species species.csv \     --species-id species --abundance cover --target elevation \     --max-epochs 100 --seed 7 --output seed_$run.pt > /dev/null   resolve predict --model seed_$run.pt --header plots.csv \     --species species.csv --species-id species --abundance cover \     --output seed_$run.csv > /dev/null done cmp seed_a.csv seed_b.csv && echo "same predictions" #> same predictions awk -F, 'NR > 1 && $2 > 47 { gsub(/"/, "", $1); print $1 }' \   plots.csv > north.txt resolve train --header plots.csv --species species.csv \   --species-id species --abundance cover --target elevation \   --stopping-plots north.txt --max-epochs 100 \   --output north.pt | grep -v "^Epoch" #> RESOLVE Training #> ================ #> Target: elevation (regression) #> Using cpu #>  #> Loading data... #> Loaded 150 plots #> Species vocabulary size: 26 #>  #> Creating model... #> Stopping fold: 43 plots from north.txt #>  #> Training... #> Early stopping at epoch 91 #>  #> ================ #> Training complete! #> Best epoch: 41 #> Training time: 1.88088s #> Effective batch size: 4096 #>  #> Final metrics: #>   elevation: #>     band_25: 0.837209 #>     band_10: 0.604651 #>     mae: 164.553 #>     rmse: 216.001 #>     r2: 0.892192 #>     smape: 0.141527 #>     band_50: 0.930233 #>  #> Saving model to: north.pt #> Done! resolve train --header plots.csv --species species.csv \   --species-id species --abundance cover --target elevation \   --max-epochs 100 --fixed-epochs 50 --test-size 0 \   --output refit.pt | grep -v "^Epoch" #> RESOLVE Training #> ================ #> Target: elevation (regression) #> Using cpu #>  #> Loading data... #> Loaded 150 plots #> Species vocabulary size: 26 #>  #> Creating model... #>  #> Training... #>  #> ================ #> Training complete! #> Best epoch: 49 #> Training time: 0.788807s #> Effective batch size: 4096 #>  #> Final metrics: #>  #> Saving model to: refit.pt #> Done!

title: The command line
text: --cv-folds N runs N-fold cross-validation final fit prints fold’s metrics mean standard deviation across folds. fold starts untrained weights, final fit afterwards run one without flag. --cv-spatial makes folds blocks --cv-lat-size --cv-lon-size degrees, needs coordinates; --cv-balance assigns blocks folds folds hold similar numbers plots. fold, Train: Test: counts give many plots trained tested ; spatial blocks folds differ size.

title: The command line
text: --checkpoint-dir makes run write best model progress file directory trains, --checkpoint-every N adds checkpoint every N epochs: --resume continues run wrote checkpoint epoch . Pass run’s data, model training flags seed, held-plots settings ones trained : --resume --cv-folds exclude .

title: The command line
text: --device selects run trains: cpu (default), cuda current GPU cuda:N GPU N. CUDA device machine error; run never falls back CPU . resolve predict takes flag also defaults CPU. GPU, batch fit memory halves batch size restarts run, --batch-size-floor. --vram-fraction caps share GPU memory run may use, leaves room desktop card; takes effect build engine’s CUDA kernels. --amp turns mixed precision. Large data GPUs covers settings.
code: resolve train --header plots.csv --species species.csv \   --species-id species --abundance cover --target elevation \   --device cuda --vram-fraction 0.8 --output model.pt

title: The command line
text: resolve predict scores header species table saved model writes one row per plot. model predicts survey’s plots . first column plot identifier, followed one column per target. classification target gets two columns: habitat holds class label habitat_code integer code model predicted. --probabilities adds one column per class probability behind code; columns one target sum one every row: checkpoint carries species, genus family vocabularies training data, new tables encoded species. also records covariate categorical columns, covariate model predicts without --covariate flags; pass rename columns, one flag per column model trained . abundance, coordinate taxonomy columns read flags given, pass resolve predict flags resolve train. --predict-batch-size sets many plots go model (4096 default). retrieval flags blend prediction labels nearest plots reference set, model’s latent representation; Predicting new plots describes . model suite directory several trained models manifest.json lists . resolve predict --suite DIR scores every target suite, combines members’ predictions reports far agree much plot’s species list target’s vocabulary recognises. --target limits output targets, --members adds every member’s prediction ---verify skips checking member file size SHA-256 checksum manifest. resolve info --suite DIR prints manifest checks every member. Predicting new plots covers suites.
code: resolve predict --model model.pt --header plots.csv --species species.csv \   --species-id species --abundance cover --genus genus --family family \   --output predictions.csv head -n 4 predictions.csv #> RESOLVE Prediction #> ================== #> Loading model from: model.pt #> Using cpu #> Loading data... #> Loaded 150 plots #> Making predictions (batch_size=4096)... #> Writing predictions to: predictions.csv #> Done! Wrote 150 predictions. #> Classification targets are written as two columns: '<target>' (class label) and '<target>_code' (integer code). #> plot_id,elevation,habitat,habitat_code #> A001,2247.743,alpine,0 #> A002,1002.3265,grassland,2 #> A003,2104.989,wetland,3 resolve predict --model model.pt --header plots.csv --species species.csv \   --species-id species --abundance cover --genus genus --family family \   --probabilities --output probabilities.csv > /dev/null head -n 4 probabilities.csv #> plot_id,elevation,habitat,habitat_code,habitat_prob_alpine,habitat_prob_forest,habitat_prob_grassland,habitat_prob_wetland #> A001,2247.743,alpine,0,0.95639765,0.010085367,0.016828658,0.016688375 #> A002,1002.3265,grassland,2,0.0067752292,0.008118316,0.9660513,0.01905505 #> A003,2104.989,wetland,3,0.030167382,0.024352005,0.037282534,0.9081981

title: The command line
text: resolve info prints checkpoint holds: run split plots, schema data trained , model, loader training settings, final metrics. first part reads: hold_out explicit run --stopping-plots random one --test-size. schema lists target task, transform, missing-label policy , classification target, class labels. listing continues every setting run ends number parameters. checkpoint loads R Python like one saved package: predicted elevations match elevation column predictions.csv .
code: resolve info --model north.pt | head -n 40 #> RESOLVE Model Information #> ========================= #> Model: north.pt #>  #> Run: #>   resolve_version: 1.1.0 #>   created_at: 2026-11-09T01:34:43Z #>   completed_at: 2026-11-09T01:34:45Z #>   train_time_seconds: 1.8808783 #>   n_plots_train: 107 #>   n_plots_test: 43 #>   hold_out: explicit #>   test_size: 0 #>   split_seed: 42 #>   best_epoch: 41 #>   total_epochs: 92 #>  #> Schema: #>   n_plots: 150 #>   n_species: 25 #>   n_species_vocab: 26 #>   has_coordinates: no #>   has_abundance: yes #>   has_taxonomy: no #>   n_genera: 0 #>   n_families: 0 #>   covariates: [] #>   categoricals: [] #>   categorical_embed_dim: 8 #>   targets: #>     - name: elevation #>       task: regression #>       transform: none #>       num_classes: 0 #>       weight: 1 #>       missing: drop #>       class_names: [] #>  #> Model Configuration: #>   Model species_encoding: hash predictor <- resolve.load("model.pt") dataset <- resolve.dataset.csv(   header = "plots.csv",   species = "species.csv",   roles = list(plot_id = "plot_id", species_id = "species",                abundance = "cover", genus = "genus", family = "family"),   vocabs = predictor$vocabs(),   config = predictor$dataset_config() ) preds <- resolve.predict.dataset(predictor, dataset) head(round(preds$predictions$elevation)) #> [1] 2248 1002 2105 2319 2004 1950 import resolve_core as rc  predictor = rc.Predictor.load("model.pt") roles = rc.RoleMapping() roles.plot_id = "plot_id" roles.species_id = "species" roles.abundance = "cover" roles.genus = "genus" roles.family = "family"  dataset = rc.ResolveDataset.from_csv_with_vocabs(     "plots.csv", "species.csv", roles, [],     predictor.external_vocabs, predictor.dataset_config) preds = predictor.predict_dataset(dataset) print(preds.predictions["elevation"][:6].round())

title: Preparing the two tables
text: role tells loader column means. plot species identifiers required; every role optional adds input model. embedding learned vector numbers stands one name, genus, family level categorical column. code: plots <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "plots.csv", package = "resolveR")) species <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "species.csv", package = "resolveR"))  roles <- list(plot_id = "plot_id", species_id = "species",               abundance = "cover", genus = "genus", family = "family") targets <- list(   elevation = list(column = "elevation", task = "regression"),   habitat = list(column = "habitat", task = "classification") ) dataset <- resolve.dataset.frame(plots, species, roles = roles,                                  targets = targets) import pandas as pd import resolve_core as rc  data = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gcol33/resolve/master/r/inst/extdata/" plots = pd.read_csv(data + "plots.csv") species = pd.read_csv(data + "species.csv")  roles = rc.RoleMapping() roles.plot_id = "plot_id" roles.species_id = "species" roles.abundance = "cover" roles.genus = "genus" roles.family = "family"  targets = [rc.TargetSpec.regression("elevation"),            rc.TargetSpec.classification("habitat", 4)] dataset = rc.ResolveDataset.from_pandas(plots, species, roles, targets)

code: fit <- resolve.train.dataset(dataset, lr = 1e-3, maxEpochs = 100L,                              trainConfig = list(weight_decay = 1e-4),                              verbose = FALSE) fit$trainer$get_config()[c("lr", "weight_decay")] #> $lr #> [1] 0.001 #>  #> $weight_decay #> [1] 1e-04 cfg = rc.TrainConfig() cfg.lr = 1e-3 cfg.weight_decay = 1e-4 cfg.max_epochs = 100 model = rc.ResolveModel(dataset.schema, rc.model_config_for_dataset(dataset)) trainer = rc.Trainer(model, cfg) trainer.prepare_data(dataset, test_size=0.2, seed=42) result = trainer.fit() round(trainer.config.lr, 6), round(trainer.config.weight_decay, 6) #> (0.001, 0.0001)

text: schedule changes rate run. default none runs rate stays lr. Four schedules available: step multiplies rate lr_gamma (default 0.1) every lr_step_size epochs (default 100). cosine lowers rate along cosine lr lr_min (default 0.000001), reached last epoch max_epochs. linear lowers rate every optimizer step lr_min end max_epochs. plateau follows held-fold lowers rate held-value stops improving. runs train fixed 100 epochs, rate history, rate epoch trained , covers whole schedule. step schedule drops rate every 30 epochs; cosine schedule ends lr_min last epoch. laid max_epochs, run early stopping ends sooner never reaches end. plateau schedule linear warmup start run covered Training reading fit.
code: step <- resolve.train.dataset(dataset, maxEpochs = 100L, fixedEpochs = 100L,                               verbose = FALSE,                               lrScheduler = "step", lrStepSize = 30L,                               lrGamma = 0.1) signif(step$result$lr[c(1, 30, 31, 61, 91)], 3) #> [1] 1e-03 1e-03 1e-04 1e-05 1e-06  cosine <- resolve.train.dataset(dataset, maxEpochs = 100L, fixedEpochs = 100L,                                 verbose = FALSE,                                 lrScheduler = "cosine", lrMin = 1e-6) signif(cosine$result$lr[c(1, 25, 50, 75, 100)], 3) #> [1] 0.001000 0.000862 0.000508 0.000150 0.000001 cfg = rc.TrainConfig() cfg.max_epochs = 100 cfg.fixed_epochs = 100 cfg.lr_scheduler = rc.LRSchedulerType.StepLR cfg.lr_step_size = 30 cfg.lr_gamma = 0.1 model = rc.ResolveModel(dataset.schema, rc.model_config_for_dataset(dataset)) step = rc.Trainer(model, cfg) step.prepare_data(dataset, test_size=0.2, seed=42) step_rates = step.fit().lr_history [float(f"{step_rates[epoch - 1]:.3g}") for epoch in [1, 30, 31, 61, 91]] #> [0.001, 0.001, 0.0001, 1e-05, 1e-06]  cfg = rc.TrainConfig() cfg.max_epochs = 100 cfg.fixed_epochs = 100 cfg.lr_scheduler = rc.LRSchedulerType.CosineAnnealing cfg.lr_min = 1e-6 model = rc.ResolveModel(dataset.schema, rc.model_config_for_dataset(dataset)) cosine = rc.Trainer(model, cfg) cosine.prepare_data(dataset, test_size=0.2, seed=42) cosine_rates = cosine.fit().lr_history [float(f"{cosine_rates[epoch - 1]:.3g}") for epoch in [1, 25, 50, 75, 100]] #> [0.001, 0.000862, 0.000508, 0.00015, 1e-06]

code: # install.packages("pak") pak::pak("gcol33/resolve/r")  # The engine library, downloaded once library(resolveR) resolve.install_backend() pip install resolve-core import json import os import tempfile  import pandas as pd import torch import resolve_core as rc  data = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gcol33/resolve/master/r/inst/extdata/" plots = pd.read_csv(data + "plots.csv") species = pd.read_csv(data + "species.csv")  roles = rc.RoleMapping() roles.plot_id = "plot_id" roles.species_id = "species" roles.abundance = "cover" roles.genus = "genus" roles.family = "family"  root = tempfile.mkdtemp() members = {} for spec in [rc.TargetSpec.regression("elevation"),              rc.TargetSpec.classification("habitat", 4)]:     dataset = rc.ResolveDataset.from_pandas(plots, species, roles, [spec])     name = spec.target_name     os.makedirs(os.path.join(root, name))     members[name] = []     for seed in (1, 2):         torch.manual_seed(seed)         config = rc.TrainConfig()         config.max_epochs = 100         trainer = rc.Trainer(rc.ResolveModel(dataset.schema), config)         trainer.prepare_data(dataset, seed=seed)         trainer.fit()         trainer.save(os.path.join(root, name, f"seed_{seed}.pt"))         members[name].append({"seed": seed, "file": f"{name}/seed_{seed}.pt"})

code: set.seed(4) survey <- function(n) {   altitude <- runif(n, 200, 1700)   uncertainty <- 10^runif(n, 0, 3.5)   wrong <- runif(n) < 0.05 + 0.15 * log10(uncertainty)   dem <- altitude + rnorm(n, 0, 2) + ifelse(wrong, rnorm(n, 0, 300), 0)   spread <- runif(n, 5, 45)   data.frame(altitude = altitude, uncertainty = uncertainty, spread = spread,              prediction = altitude + rnorm(n, 0, spread),              dem = dem, dem_1km = dem + rnorm(n, 0, 15)) } recorded <- survey(6000) new_plots <- survey(2000) c(prediction = mean(abs(new_plots$prediction - new_plots$altitude)),   elevation_model = mean(abs(new_plots$dem - new_plots$altitude))) #>      prediction elevation_model  #>        19.59923        77.21113 import numpy as np import torch import resolve_core as rc  rng = np.random.default_rng(4)   def survey(n):     altitude = rng.uniform(200, 1700, n)     uncertainty = 10 ** rng.uniform(0, 3.5, n)     wrong = rng.random(n) < 0.05 + 0.15 * np.log10(uncertainty)     dem = altitude + rng.normal(0, 2, n) + np.where(wrong, rng.normal(0, 300, n), 0)     spread = rng.uniform(5, 45, n)     t = lambda x: torch.tensor(x, dtype=torch.float64)     return dict(altitude=t(altitude), uncertainty_m=t(uncertainty), spread=t(spread),                 prediction=t(altitude + rng.normal(0, spread)), dem=t(dem),                 dem_1km=t(dem + rng.normal(0, 15, n)))   recorded = survey(6000) new_plots = survey(2000) mae = lambda x: (x - new_plots["altitude"]).abs().mean().item() print(f"prediction {mae(new_plots['prediction']):.1f} m, elevation model {mae(new_plots['dem']):.1f} m") #> prediction 19.6 m, elevation model 73.1 m path <- file.path(tempdir(), "altitude.terrain") report <- resolve.fit_terrain_correction(   "altitude", "elevation", recorded$prediction, recorded$dem, recorded$altitude, path,   dem1km = recorded$dem_1km, uncertainty = recorded$uncertainty, spread = recorded$spread,   config = list(scale = 500, epochs = 80L, batch_size = 256L)) corrected <- resolve.terrain_correction(path, new_plots$prediction, new_plots$dem,                                         dem1km = new_plots$dem_1km,                                         uncertainty = new_plots$uncertainty,                                         spread = new_plots$spread) mean(abs(corrected$corrected - new_plots$altitude)) #> [1] 8.95824 import os, tempfile  cfg = rc.TerrainCorrectionConfig() cfg.scale, cfg.epochs, cfg.batch_size = 500.0, 80, 256 inputs = lambda s: {k: v for k, v in s.items() if k != "altitude"} model = rc.fit_terrain_correction("altitude", rc.TerrainDescriptor.Elevation,                                   truth=recorded["altitude"], config=cfg, **inputs(recorded)) model.save(os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "altitude.terrain")) corrected = model.apply(**inputs(new_plots)) print(f"corrected {mae(corrected.corrected):.1f} m") #> corrected 8.2 m precision <- cut(new_plots$uncertainty, c(0, 10, 100, 1000, Inf),                  labels = c("up to 10 m", "10-100 m", "100 m-1 km", "over 1 km")) round(aggregate(corrected$weights, list(uncertainty = precision), mean)[, -1], 2) #>   resolve  dem dem_1km #> 1    0.13 0.86    0.00 #> 2    0.26 0.73    0.00 #> 3    0.38 0.62    0.01 #> 4    0.51 0.48    0.01 w = corrected.weights.numpy() u = new_plots["uncertainty_m"].numpy() for label, lo, hi in [("up to 10 m", 0, 10), ("10-100 m", 10, 100),                       ("100 m-1 km", 100, 1000), ("over 1 km", 1000, np.inf)]:     m = (u > lo) & (u <= hi)     print(label, np.round(w[m].mean(axis=0), 2)) #> up to 10 m [0.14 0.84 0.01] #> 10-100 m [0.22 0.76 0.01] #> 100 m-1 km [0.37 0.62 0.02] #> over 1 km [0.49 0.5  0.01]
